hints: Look closely at the conditions, cold and dilute means a very mild oxidation, not vigorous cleavage.
Draw out pent-2-ene as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and notice the C=C bond between C2 and C3 is where reaction happens.
Think about adding one -OH group to each carbon of the double bond to form a diol, and see which formula matches that pattern.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two manganate(VII) alkene reactions**

Manganate(VII) can do two very different jobs depending on conditions. Cold, dilute conditions give mild oxidation to a diol. Hot, concentrated conditions give vigorous oxidative cleavage of the C=C bond.

Rule:
$$\text{alkene + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{cold, dilute } \text{MnO}_4^-} \text{diol}$$

**Apply mild hydroxylation to pent-2-ene**

Pent-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Each carbon of the C=C gets one -OH added across the double bond.

Reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{[O]} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Identify the major product**

The product has -OH groups on C2 and C3, which is pentane-2,3-diol. That is exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$ written in a different order.

options.A: Correct. Cold, dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ adds two -OH groups syn across the double bond to give the 2,3-diol. For pent-2-ene this is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCOCH}_3$ is a diketone. Cold dilute manganate does not oxidise alkenes to carbonyls, it stops at the diol stage.
options.C: Incorrect. These are the two isomeric secondary alcohols from acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov addition of water). That needs concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ then water, not cold dilute $\text{MnO}_4^-$, and it adds only one -OH, not two.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ are cleavage products from breaking the C=C bond. This is the classic trap, it requires hot, concentrated acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ with strong heating, not cold dilute conditions.
